baseline.name: Sequential target search
baseline.approach: Inspect sorted entries from the beginning until finding or passing the target.

why: Sorted order lets each midpoint comparison discard roughly half of the remaining candidates.
quantitative_comparison: For n>=1, binary search performs at most floor(log2(n))+1 loop iterations versus up to n inspected entries in sequential search. For n=1024 that is at most 11 iterations versus 1024 entries; these different operations are not a measured speed ratio.
tradeoffs: Requires random-access sorted data. A small or cache-friendly sequential search may still be faster on a particular host; duplicate targets need not return the first position.
evidence_basis: Static interval-halving comparison with explicit size/count model; no runtime benchmark.
